pillar_reactions.evidence: Delivered at length and aimed at his constraints — no gym required, 30 to 40 minutes three or four times a week, five to ten minutes of daily mobility to undo years of sitting. The prospect's engagement took the form of practical questions rather than enthusiasm: 'And these workouts are from the home you said, right? You don't have to go to the gym?' and 'I do have like one or two kettlebells at home, 35 pounds, 15 pounds, 10 pounds. What else do you need in terms of the equipment for this?' At the close of the call he gave the clearest positive signal of the session when asked what stood out: 'rather than just going to the gym, you're going to set up your foundations with this. I think that is something I'm more interested to learn' and 'having the flexibility to work out any way, everything, just one kettlebell is also something interesting.'

Built around intermittent fasting, which was well chosen given he already fasts and named it as his most effective lever. The delivery included a direct challenge to his big-boned framing — 'oftentimes the people that say they're big boned, when we actually look at their diet and count the macros, well, they're eating in a calorie surplus, that's, it's science.' His reaction was minimal: 'No, I think, I think I'm good.' He raised no questions and no objection, and immediately afterwards flagged his hard stop. Notable that this pillar contained the call's most questionable claim, that within an eating window 'you can eat as much as you freaking want, and it becomes almost impossible to actually overeat', which drew no reaction either.

Never delivered. The call ran out of time after training and nutrition and was rescheduled. This is the single most consequential omission on the call: accountability is the mechanism this prospect identified as the one thing missing from every previous attempt — 'by the time that camp ends, obviously, there's no one holding you accountable at that point. And then you just let loose' and 'if someone is holding me accountable or just checking up on me that kind of gives me a little bit of motivation.' The pillar that directly answers his stated root cause is the pillar he has not heard.

anchors.raw: I've done bootcamps, right. Um, a lot of bootcamps... in six-week bootcamps, ended up losing, like, 20 points and stuff like that, which is a big encouragement for me... Bootcamps actually really helped me, to be honest with you, because you're doing in a group setting, and then there's some competition there.
anchors.competitor: Local six-week bootcamps, repeated over several years
anchors.note: No price was named on either side, so this is provisional, but the format anchor is strong and works against a six-month commitment: he has repeatedly bought short, cheap, group-based programmes that produce fast visible results, and he liked them. The rep addressed this well and early by reframing the six-week cycle as the cause of the relapse rather than the solution — 'you can see a bit of a transformation in six weeks, but to really have that identity level shift... that takes a lot longer.' Whether that survives contact with a $6,000 price is the open question for Wednesday.

anchors.raw: I also had a trainer in the past, I'd go one, three sessions, but everyone, everything I feel like commercial, right? At this point, mean, 30-minute session, you're done, and basically, there is no checking back type of thing. So I really didn't like the trainer aspect of the gym.
anchors.note: He has already ruled out the obvious cheaper substitute and named the exact reason — no follow-up between sessions — which is precisely what the accountability pillar sells. This is the strongest available support for the price and, because the call ended before that pillar, it has not yet been connected to anything.

anchors.raw: if I tell you that I was 253 pounds last month, I was 253 pounds last month… 268 to 270 right now. So I gained like, within a month.
anchors.note: Not a price anchor but a decision anchor, and an unusually urgent one: he watched fifteen pounds return in four weeks and described the pattern as accelerating. The cost of a further year of this is concrete and quantified in his own numbers, which is the strongest material available for the consequence frame that was only partially run.

unmet_demand.want: To gain enough muscle while losing weight to avoid ending up with loose skin again. Raised twice and named as a primary reason he hesitates to lose weight at all: 'I want something where I can actually gain muscle while losing weight at the same time so that I don't lose weight too' and 'I got really insecure with those, with that loose skin.'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme genuinely cannot deliver it at an 80 lb loss and the rep said so directly rather than selling around it: 'There's not going to be an amount of muscle that's going to fill in all the fat that you have right now. It's just not going to happen. Unfortunately.' He then set the expectation of an uncomfortable interim phase. That is honest handling of a real product limit and should be recorded as such, but the want remains unmet and it is a live risk to retention — loose-skin insecurity is what he says derailed him last time.

unmet_demand.want: To come off blood pressure medication, which he named as his single biggest goal, and to stop needing CPAP for sleep apnea.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Neither was addressed at any point after being raised in the first six minutes. The rep did not claim the programme would achieve either, which is the correct restraint, but he also did not say anything about how weight loss interacts with either condition, whether the programme accommodates them, or whether a clinician should be involved in any decision to reduce medication. The prospect's primary goal was left entirely unanswered.

unmet_demand.want: Programming that works around two years of knee problems, a restricted shoulder and chronic lower back weakness — he cannot run or jump and flags that misalignment restarts his back pain.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Answered with a general claim rather than a plan: 'it can be worked around basically any starting points' followed by a personal anecdote and the prediction that 'the stuff with the knees, like a lot of that's going to start going away in a very short period of time.' Nothing about assessment, load management or substitution, and no suggestion of clinical input. Recorded here as unvalidated and separately as a critical integrity flag.

unmet_demand.want: Material to review between calls. Asked for twice — 'if you want to share something in the meantime, I can go through it offline. And then when we connect, it will be quicker.'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: None exists in a form the rep could send. 'I don't really have any, like, materials. Usually, I just talk through everything.' He re-texted the existing content page, which is marketing video rather than programme information. This is the second call in this batch where a prospect asked for something to read or hand on and there was nothing to give them, which points to a missing asset rather than a rep failure.

unmet_demand.want: A visible path from 268 lb to the goal that does not look impossible. He named the scale of the journey as the thing that defeats him: 'the biggest discouragement for me is just seeing my journey, like how I'm going to achieve that big goal.'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Partially served. The rep addressed the identity and timeframe question well and reframed six-week cycles as the cause of relapse, which is the right argument. What was not offered was any staged or milestone structure that makes an 80 lb goal legible, and the delivery walkthrough that might have contained it was not reached before the call ended.
